content: Acoustic stimulation of the fetus has been proposed as a method to enhance the efficiency of fetal heart rate testing conducted during pregnancy. The objective of this study was to evaluate both the benefits and potential drawbacks of using fetal vibroacoustic stimulation in combination with tests designed to assess fetal wellbeing. A comprehensive search was conducted within the Cochrane Pregnancy and Childbirth Group's Trials Register up to September 30, 2013. The study included all randomized controlled trials, both published and unpublished, that investigated the effectiveness of fetal vibroacoustic stimulation when used alongside tests of fetal wellbeing. Data extraction and trial quality assessment were performed independently by all review authors. Additionally, the authors of the included trials were contacted to obtain further information when necessary. A total of 12 trials involving 6,822 participants were included in the analysis. The use of fetal vibroacoustic stimulation was found to significantly reduce the occurrence of non-reactive results in antenatal cardiotocography tests. Specifically, data from nine trials demonstrated an average risk ratio (RR) of 0.62, with a 95% confidence interval (CI) ranging from 0.48 to 0.81. Furthermore, when compared to mock stimulation, vibroacoustic stimulation elicited a significantly higher number of fetal movements during fetal heart rate testing, as evidenced by one trial (RR 0.23, 95% CI 0.18 to 0.29). The authors concluded that vibroacoustic stimulation provides measurable benefits, including a reduction in the incidence of non-reactive cardiotocography results and a decrease in the time required for testing. However, they emphasized the need for further randomized trials to determine the optimal parameters for vibroacoustic stimulation, such as intensity, frequency, duration, and positioning. Additionally, future research should focus on evaluating the efficacy, predictive reliability, safety, and perinatal outcomes associated with the use of vibroacoustic stimulation in conjunction with cardiotocography and other fetal wellbeing assessments.
